explain: Each band links a source to a destination. Its thickness is the amount. The blocks are the sources, the intermediate steps and the destinations.
Hover over a block or a band to highlight the flows that go through it and read their amount.

currency.title: Wealth by currency
currency.summary: The value of your wealth in the currencies of your choice (euro, dollar, Swiss franc, baht…), month by month.
currency.source: history table: Date and the amounts in euros (Assets Master Currency, Liabilities Master Currency), converted by the site into each currency at the ECB rate of the record’s date, or a currency column of the sheet (EUR, USD…). Added up by date.
explain: For each month, one bar per ticked currency gives the total value of your wealth expressed in that currency. This isn’t a breakdown: it’s the same wealth, converted into each currency.
So the bars move together; the gap between them only changes with exchange rates. A month’s amount is that of the last record of the month.
Tick the currencies to show above the chart, or add one with “Add a currency”: your choice is saved (to your account if you are signed in).
Amounts in other currencies are calculated by the site with the European Central Bank (ECB) reference rates, on the date of each record. Your sheet only needs the amounts in euros.
currency.noColumn: No amount per currency in the “{table}” table: it needs the Assets Master Currency column (or an EUR, USD… column) and ECB rates in the database. Available columns: {available}.
currency.a11y: Wealth in {codes} from {from} to {to}: {amounts} in the last month.

allocation.a11y: Breakdown by asset type from {from} to {to}. In the last month, {asset} makes up {share}.
allocation.title: Breakdown by asset type, month by month
allocation.summary: The share of each asset type in your wealth, each month.
allocation.source: history table, columns Date, Asset and Assets Master Currency (amounts above 0), last record of each month.
explain: Each bar is 100% of your wealth at the end of a month, split by asset type. The colours are those of the asset type ring.
Amounts follow the Gross / Net button in the menu: in gross, debts don’t count; in net, each debt is taken off its asset type. Hover over a bar to read the share and amount of each type.

assets.a11y: Lines for {count} asset types from {from} to {to}. Total in the last month: {total}.
assets.title: Change by asset type
assets.summary: The amount of each asset type, month after month.
assets.source: history table, columns Date, Asset and Assets Master Currency (amounts above 0), last record of each month.
explain: Each line follows one asset type, in the same colour as in the other charts. It rises when you invest or the market goes up, and falls when the market goes down or you withdraw.
Hover over a month: the tooltip ranks asset types from largest to smallest. Clicking a name in the legend hides or shows its line.

variation.a11y: Monthly change in wealth from {from} to {to}. Last month: {last}.
variation.title: Monthly change
variation.summary: How much your wealth goes up or down, in %, from one month to the next.
variation.source: history table, columns Date and Assets Master Currency, added up by date; last record of each month.
explain: Each bar compares the total of your wealth (gross or net, depending on the menu button) at the end of a month with the previous month. Blue bars above zero are rises; orange bars below are falls.
This change mixes two causes: what you put in or took out, and what the market did. Separating them needs the inout tab, which isn’t used here yet.

inout.a11y: Monthly bars from {from} to {to}: {in} in and {out} out in total.
inout.a11yTax: Monthly bars from {from} to {to}: {in} in, {out} out and {tax} in taxes in total.
inout.title: Inflows, outflows and taxes
inout.summary: The money you put in, take out and pay in taxes, month by month.
inout.source: inout table, columns date, in, out and tax. Outflows and taxes entered as negative numbers are counted as absolute values.
explain: For each month, the blue bar totals the money put into your investments (in), the orange bar the money taken out (out) and the yellow bar the taxes (tax). Months without movement show as zero.
The month’s net (inflows minus outflows and taxes) is shown in the tooltip and in the table view. It explains the part of the monthly change that doesn’t come from the market.

trend.title: Wealth and trend
trend.summary: Your wealth in {currency} at each record, with the trend line.
trend.source: history table, Date column and the amount column of the currency chosen in the header (EUR by default, otherwise Assets Master Currency), added up by date. Rows without Asset or Instrument are goals.
explain: Each bar is the total of your wealth in {currency} (gross or net, depending on the menu button) on a record date. The line is the average trend of all records: it shows your past growth rate.

The orange diamonds are your goals: in the history table, they are the rows that have only a date and an amount (no asset type, no instrument). The trend is extended as a dotted line to the last goal: if it passes above a diamond, your current pace is enough to reach it.
Goals stretch the time axis: the slider at the bottom lets you zoom in on the records.

envelopeTypes.title: ETFs, shares and cash by envelope
envelopeTypes.summary: What each envelope holds: ETFs, shares, cash…
explain: One bar per investment envelope, split by sub-type (ETF, share, cash waiting to be invested…). The total is written at the end of the bar.
It matches the “etf_pea/cto” and “action_pea/cto” charts of the old Data Studio report.

envelopeAreas.title: Geographic areas by envelope
envelopeAreas.summary: The country or area of what each envelope holds.
explain: One bar per investment envelope, split by country or area (Area column of your sheet). A world ETF goes in the area you gave it.
It matches the “pee/per” and “pea/cto” by-country charts of the old Data Studio report.

envelopeInstruments.title: Envelopes and instruments
envelopeInstruments.summary: The weight of each investment envelope, and what it holds.
envelopeInstruments.source: portfolio table, columns Envelope (or Account), Instrument, Ticker and Assets Master Currency, at the last record. Only envelopes that hold shares, ETFs or funds are kept.
explain: The inner ring shows the weight of each investment envelope (brokerage account, PEA, PER, PEE…). The outer ring details what it holds, instrument by instrument, in shades of the same colour.

Each instrument is named by its Instrument column followed by its ticker (“MSCI world · UETW”). Hover over a slice to read its amount, its share of the total and its share of the envelope; the table view lists them all.
Instruments that weigh less than 1% of their envelope (often cash waiting to be invested) are grouped under “Others”.

envelopeHistory.title: Change in each envelope
envelopeHistory.summary: The amount in each investment envelope, month after month.
envelopeHistory.source: history table, columns Date, Envelope (or Account), Asset and Assets Master Currency; last record of each month. The envelopes kept are those holding shares, ETFs or funds at the last record.
explain: One line per investment envelope, at the last record of each month. It rises when you invest or the market goes up.
Clicking a name in the legend hides or shows its line; the tooltip ranks envelopes from largest to smallest.

volatility.title: Over {period}
volatility.summary: How much the price of each of your investments moved over {period}.
volatility.explain1: One bubble per investment. Horizontally, the amount you hold (log scale: each tick multiplies by 10); vertically, the change in its unit price over {period}. The bigger the bubble, the more the investment weighs in your wealth.
volatility.explain2: The unit price is calculated in {currency} (amount ÷ quantity): it accounts for exchange rates, but not for your purchases or sales. A big bubble far below the zero line is the investment that lost you the most.
volatility.explain3: Cash, real estate and assets without a market price aren’t shown.
volatility.source: history table with your current positions (portfolio tab), columns Date, Instrument, Quantity, Assets Master Currency (and Asset, Envelope, Broker if present): current prices compared with those on the same day {period} earlier.

sheet.q: What should my Google Sheet contain?
sheet.a: Overfolio looks for five tabs by name: portfolio, inout, stock, budget and history. Each page lists the columns it needs. If one is missing, the page tells you which, and the other pages keep working.

access.q: Can Overfolio change my sheet or see my bank accounts?
access.a: No. Overfolio connects to no bank: it only reads the sheet you share with it, without writing anything. The rows it reads are copied into its database so the pages load fast. If you stop sharing in Google Sheets, Overfolio can no longer read it.

update.a: On demand. On the GoogleSheet page, the Refresh all button rereads all your tabs. The date and time of the last sync stay visible, and every chart shows the date of its data.

advice.q: Does Overfolio tell me what to buy or sell?
advice.a: No. Overfolio shows what’s in your sheet: it recommends no investment. The Simulation page projects scenarios from your own assumptions, without predicting anything. Its charts help you see the big picture before you make your own decisions.

subAssetPerformance.title: Price change by sub-type
subAssetPerformance.summary: How much the price of your stocks, ETFs, bitcoin, gold… has moved over the chosen periods, in days.
explain: One bar per period chosen above the chart, for each investment sub-type (Sub Asset column). ETFs are split by instrument: ETF msci world, ETF dbmfe…
A sub-type’s change is the change in its value at constant quantities: today’s quantities, at the current price and at the start date’s price. Your purchases and sales therefore don’t count.

The current price comes from the portfolio tab. The start date’s price is estimated between the two history records around it, pro rata by day: over a short period, it is an estimate. Cash, real estate and goods without a market price are not counted.
subAssetPerformance.source: history table with your current positions (portfolio tab), columns Date, Sub Asset, Instrument, Quantity, Assets Master Currency (and Account, Broker if present).

flowPage.yearNote: Only {year} records and movements are shown: January’s change isn’t calculated, since there’s no December record in the period, and the trend covers that year only.
flowPage.footer: The charts read the database. To update it from your sheet, use the Refresh all button on the {sheet} page. For your wealth today, open {snapshot}.

volatilityPage.lead: How much the price of each of your investments has moved. One bubble per investment: what you hold most is on the right, what fell most is at the bottom. Prices are in {currency}, exchange rates included, excluding your purchases and sales.
volatilityPage.footer: Changes compare your current prices (portfolio tab) with those on the same day 1 month, 3 months or 1 year earlier, or over any other period chosen at the top of the page. As the history table has only one record a month, those earlier prices are estimated between the two records around that date: the more records you keep, the more precise they are.

Link with shares: 1 = moves exactly with the stock market, 0 = unrelated, negative = tends to rise when it falls. Contributions are split between the ticked types, in proportion to their amounts.

a11y.link: Link of {asset} with shares, from -1 to 1

limits: No tax on withdrawal (PEA, brokerage account and PER are taxed differently): amounts are before tax.
No rebalancing: the allocation drifts over the draws, as if you never sold.
Default returns are long-term orders of magnitude, not promises: change them.
Your sheet’s recent past (about two years) is too short to derive returns from: it isn’t used for the assumptions.
simulationPage.notAdvice: This is a projection tool, not investment advice.
simulationPage.noPositive: The portfolio table has no positive amount in Assets Master Currency.
